pages.name: A2
pages.title: Background Knowledge of Google My Activity Dashboard

elements.name: A2_intro_MyActivity
elements.html:
In the following section, we will ask you some general questions to learn more about your knowledge of the Google “My Activity” dashboard in general and your usage of this feature in particular.

The Google “My Activity” dashboard is a service provided by Google that allows users to view, manage, and delete the activity data collected from their use of various Google services (such as Search, YouTube, Maps, Chrome, and more). “My Activity” organizes your past activity in a timeline and gives you control over what data is stored in your Google Account.

  • You can access the Google “My Activity” dashboard by visiting https://myactivity.google.com/ while signed into your Google Account.
  • You can also find it by going to your Google Account → Data & Privacy → History settings → My Activity.
  • “My Activity” allows you to view activity by date, Google product, and category. You can also delete specific items, delete activity in bulk, or turn on auto-delete for future activity.
You can learn more about the Google “My Activity” dashboard from the official help page: Click here

pages.name: A3
pages.title: Opinions about Activity Collection and Personalization

elements.name: A3_T1
elements.html: During the rest of this survey, we use the term “activity data” to refer to the records a company (e.g., Google) keeps of what you searched for, watched, visited, or did while using its services.

elements.noneText: I don’t think Google collects data across services

elements.name: A5_T1
elements.html:
In the following section, we will ask you some questions to learn more about your usage of the Google “My Activity” dashboard, as well as how you interact with Google services that contribute to your stored activity. We will also ask a few questions regarding your cross-device Google usage.

A Google activity log refers to the information collected by Google based on your interactions with its products and services. This may include your searches, websites visited, apps used, videos watched, voice and audio interactions, location history, and other related activities. Activity logs may include timestamps, device details, product information, and, in some cases, content associated with your activity (e.g., what you searched for or watched). These activity logs are stored in your Google “My Activity” dashboard and may differ across devices and products. (See the figure below)

Figure: Example representation of Google activity logs

Below is some brief information to help you understand where activity logs come from and how they are stored:

  • Google stores activity when you use services such as Search, YouTube, Maps, Chrome, and others while signed into your Google Account.
  • Activity may also be stored from multiple devices simultaneously if the same Google Account is signed in.
  • You can view, delete, or manage these activities by visiting https://myactivity.google.com.

elements.name: A5_T2
elements.html:
Before continuing, please complete a few quick tasks on your Google “My Activity” dashboard (https://myactivity.google.com) to help you recall what’s stored in your account.

  1. Visit your dashboard — scroll through your recent activity.
  2. Filter by category — use “Filter by date & product” to check at least 3 different Google products.
  3. Filter by time — view activity for Today, Yesterday, and Last 30 days.
